paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people living in Barnet, and they include Barnet Council's own fostering service as well as independent agencies. Fostering for the council means caring for Barnet's own children with its social workers supporting you; an independent agency assesses, trains and supervises you itself and is asked by councils to find homes for children they look after.

Barnet does not recruit on its own. It is one of six councils, with Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey and Islington, in the North London Fostering Hub, which Camden hosts. The hub grew out of the North London Fostering and Permanency Consortium, through which the six boroughs have shared training, resources and recruitment since 2012, and its stated aim is to help more children stay near their schools, friends and support networks. Camden's announcement also says the government's Room Makers programme, which helps carers fund changes to their homes so they can take more children, is being extended to every fostering hub.

Barnet's financial policy for foster and connected carers, dated April 2024, pays two weekly amounts: a maintenance allowance for each child, set at £191 for babies up to two rising to £289 for 16 and 17-year-olds, and a skills fee of £181, £211 or £289 depending on level, reviewed at each annual review. On top of that it sets out birthday, festival and holiday payments, a uniform allowance, and an enhanced payment for out-of-hours placements. Carers placed through the north London partnership are paid at Barnet's rates. Rates are reviewed, so ask the council for the current figures.

Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before you decide, and compare training, support and pay. If you live near the borough's edge, the pages for Enfield, Haringey and London as a whole list more services.
